newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND'S STEWART HEADS FOR 200 VS NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND'S STEWART HEADS FOR 200 VS NZ.

text.p: England batsman Alec Stewart was setting his sights on a double century at tea on the third day of the first cricket test against New Zealand on Sunday.
At the interval, Stewart was on 165 as England reached 285 for three in reply to New Zealand's first innings 390.
Stewart reached 150 off 254 balls, with 20 fours and one six. He has now scored centuries on all three major New Zealand test grounds.
He hit 148 at Lancaster Park in Christchurch and 107 at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on the 1991-92 tour. It is his fourth century in tests against New Zealand, and his 10th overall.
Stewart lost two partners in the middle session.
England captain Mike Atherton made 83 before he slammed offspinner Dipak Patel back down the offside of the pitch.
Justin Vaughan, fielding at shortish mid on, palmed the ball up and Patel grabbed the deflection.
Atherton, putting a bad run slump in Zimbabwe and New Zealand behind him, batted 273 minutes, faced 213 balls and hit 11 boundaries. He shared a 182-run stand with Stewart in 377 balls.
Nasser Hussain didn't last long before being caught at silly point off Patel for eight.
At tea, Stewart and Thorpe had added 63 in 84 minutes for the fourth wicket.
